lessons.title: Word and PowerPoint Basics
lessons.notes_html:
Headers and footers in Word

A header is text or a number printed at the top of every page, and a footer is the same kind of text printed at the bottom of every page. They are used for things that repeat on all pages, such as the document title, the page number or the date, so they do not have to be typed on each page again.

Types of text alignment in Word

Left alignment lines up text at the left margin and leaves the right edge uneven; it is the usual default. Centre alignment puts each line in the middle of the page, which suits titles. Right alignment lines up text at the right margin, and Justified alignment spreads each line so both the left and right edges are straight, which suits formal paragraphs.

Inserting an image into a PowerPoint slide

Click on the slide, go to the Insert tab and choose Pictures, then pick the image file and click Insert. The picture appears on the slide, where it can be moved, resized by dragging its corners, and placed neatly beside the text.

Transitions and animations compared

A transition is the effect that happens when the show moves from one slide to the next, for example Fade or Push. An animation is an effect on a single object on a slide, such as a title flying in or a shape spinning. In short, transitions act on whole slides, while animations act on objects inside a slide.

Adding bullet points to a slide

Click inside the text box, go to the Home tab and click the Bullets button, then type each point on a new line. Each line then starts with a bullet dot, which makes a list of points easy to read at a glance.

Two ways to save a presentation

First, press Ctrl + S (or click File, then Save) to save the presentation in its PowerPoint (.pptx) form so it can be edited again later. Second, use File, then Export or Save As, to save it in another form, for example as a video (.mp4) or a PDF, for sharing or showing without editing.

The purpose of the Slide Master

The Slide Master holds the design that all slides follow: the background, colours, fonts and the places for titles and text. Changing the master changes every slide at once, so the whole presentation keeps one consistent layout and theme instead of each slide looking different.

The purpose of a table in Word

A table arranges information in rows and columns, for example a class timetable with days across the top and periods down the side. This keeps facts neat, lined up and easy to compare, which is much clearer than writing the same facts as a long paragraph.

lessons.title: Word and PowerPoint in Depth
lessons.notes_html:
Word and PowerPoint compared

Microsoft Word is a word-processing program for writing and formatting text documents, and it is best for assignments, reports, letters and any work that is mainly read page by page. PowerPoint is a presentation program for making slides, and it is best for showing ideas to an audience with short text, pictures, tables, charts and spoken explanation. Word suits detailed written work, while PowerPoint suits short visual points talked through in front of others.

Formatting a document in Word, step by step

Step 1: Type the text, then select the part to change.

Step 2: Set the font, size and style (bold, italic or underline) from the Home tab.

Step 3: Set the alignment (left, centre, right or justified) and the line spacing so the text is easy to read.

Step 4: Add headings, bullet lists, page numbers and a header or footer if needed.

Step 5: Check spelling with the Review tab and save the document with Ctrl + S.

How SmartArt and Charts improve a presentation

SmartArt turns a list or a process into a diagram, such as steps in a cycle or parts of a whole, so the audience grasps the idea at a glance instead of reading a wall of text. Charts turn numbers into bars, pies or lines, so a comparison or a trend is seen at once. Together they make the message clearer, quicker to understand and more interesting to watch.

Applying transitions and animations

To apply a transition, select a slide, open the Transitions tab, pick an effect such as Fade or Push, and set its duration; click Apply to All to use the same transition on every slide. To apply an animation, click the object on the slide, open the Animations tab and pick an entrance, emphasis, exit or motion-path effect, then set its timing and order in the Animation Pane. Preview the show to check the effects, and keep them simple and smooth so the presentation still looks professional.

Why consistent themes and layouts matter

A consistent theme (the same colours, fonts and background) and the same layouts on every slide make the presentation look neat and professional, and the audience can follow the content instead of being distracted by changing designs. It also saves time, because the Slide Master sets the design once for all slides. A presentation that keeps changing style looks untidy and makes the speaker look unprepared, while a consistent one keeps attention on the message.

lessons.title: Key Facts
lessons.notes_html:
• The main function of an Arduino microcontroller is to control electronic components based on programming.
  • A buzzer in an Arduino project produces sound when a high signal (5V) is sent to its pin.
  • A 220-ohm resistor is used in an LED circuit to protect the LED from excessive current.
  • In an Arduino sketch, setup() runs only once when the program starts.
  • The Serial Monitor in the Arduino IDE monitors sensor data in real time.
  • An LED connected backward in a circuit will not turn on.
  • On a four-band resistor, red as the third band means multiply by 100 (10 to the power 2).
  • A resistor with the bands yellow, violet, orange and gold has a resistance of 47,000 ohms (47 kilo-ohms).
  • A tolerance of plus or minus 10% is represented by the colour silver.
  • Green as the third band of a resistor is the multiplier 10 to the power 5 (100,000).

lessons.title: Arduino Components and Circuits
lessons.notes_html:
The Arduino Uno board

The Arduino Uno is a small, low-cost microcontroller board that can be programmed to control lights, motors, buzzers and sensors. It is commonly used because it is easy to program with the Arduino IDE, it has ready digital and analog pins for connecting parts, and it lets students build and test real circuits without soldering.

The function of a resistor

A resistor limits the electric current flowing in a circuit. In an LED circuit it stops too much current from reaching the LED, which would damage or burn it; for example a 220-ohm resistor keeps the LED at a safe brightness.

Digital and analog pins

Digital pins work with only two states, HIGH (5V, on) or LOW (0V, off), and are used for things like LEDs and buzzers. Analog pins can read a range of changing values, such as the varying signal from a light or temperature sensor, so they suit measurements that are not simply on or off.

Decoding a resistor: orange, white, black, silver

Step 1: Orange is the first digit, 3.

Step 2: White is the second digit, 9, giving 39.

Step 3: Black is the multiplier, times 1, giving 39 x 1 = 39 ohms.

Step 4: Silver is the tolerance, plus or minus 10%. So the resistor is 39 ohms, plus or minus 10%.

How the HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor measures distance

The sensor sends out a short burst of ultrasound and waits for the echo to bounce back from an object. It measures the time the echo takes to return, and distance is worked out from that time: distance = (time x speed of sound) divided by 2, halved because the sound travels to the object and back.

The pinMode function

It sets digital pin 13 to work as an output, so the program can send a signal out of that pin. After this, digitalWrite(13, HIGH) can switch on an LED or buzzer connected to pin 13, and digitalWrite(13, LOW) can switch it off.

Why a breadboard is used

A breadboard lets parts be pushed in and changed quickly without soldering, so a circuit can be built, tested and corrected in minutes. Direct connections are fiddly and hard to change, while a breadboard keeps wiring tidy, lets parts be reused, and makes mistakes easy to find and fix.

The Serial Monitor and debugging

The Serial Monitor shows messages and sensor values sent from the Arduino to the computer in real time. When a program misbehaves, printing values there shows what the board is actually reading and doing, so a wrong reading, a loose wire or a logic mistake can be found instead of guessed at.

lessons.title: Circuits, Code and Troubleshooting
lessons.notes_html:
Labelling an Arduino circuit diagram

  • Arduino board: the blue board on the left, which runs the program.
  • Breadboard: the white board with rows of holes on the right, which holds the circuit.
  • LED: the small red lamp pushed into the breadboard; it lights when its pin is HIGH.
  • Resistor: the small striped part in series with the LED, which limits its current.
  • Jumper wires: the coloured wires linking the two boards and the parts.
  • Digital pin: the pin header on the Arduino where a jumper wire carries the on/off signal to the LED.
  • Power (5V and GND): the 5V and GND pins at the bottom of the Arduino, linked by the red and black wires, which supply power to the breadboard circuit.

Debugging the blink program: the corrected code

void setup() {

pinMode(9, OUTPUT);

}

void loop() {

digitalWrite(9, HIGH);

delay(1000);

digitalWrite(9, LOW);

delay(1000);

}

A note on the errors

The book says the program contains three errors, but on the printed code only one syntax error is visible - the missing semicolon after the second delay(1000). The pin setup, the HIGH/LOW logic and the delays are all correct for an LED on pin 9, so no other change is needed; the corrected code above is the complete fix.

Why the correction was necessary

Every Arduino statement must end with a semicolon, so without it the program will not compile and nothing will run.

If the delay lines are removed

If the delay(1000); lines were removed, the LED would switch on and off thousands of times a second, far too fast for the eye to see, so it would look steadily lit (and dimmer) instead of blinking once a second.

Troubleshooting a faulty buzzer circuit: three possible mistakes

  • The Trig and Echo wires are swapped in the code or on the board, so the sensor never sends or never hears the pulse properly.
  • A loose or wrong wire on the sensor (5V, GND, Trig or Echo in the wrong row of the breadboard) or on the buzzer, so the readings are garbage.
  • The code uses the wrong pins for Trig/Echo, or the distance formula is wrong (for example the echo time is not halved), so the Serial Monitor values do not match the real distance and the buzzer condition never triggers.

Step-by-step fix

Step 1: First check every wire against the plan and re-seat loose jumpers.

Step 2: Then confirm the code pins match the wired pins (Trig 9, Echo 10, buzzer 7).

Step 3: Then print the raw echo time and the worked distance on the Serial Monitor and test at a known distance, such as 20 cm.

Step 4: Finally check the buzzer alone with a simple HIGH/LOW test.

The corrected circuit, described

Arduino 5V to sensor VCC and GND to sensor GND; Arduino pin 9 to sensor Trig and pin 10 to sensor Echo; Arduino pin 7 to the buzzer positive and buzzer negative to GND; all parts sharing the same GND rail on the breadboard.

mcqs.q: In the circuit diagram, the resistor is placed in series with the LED in order to do what?
options: Produce sound for the circuit
Limit the LED's current
Store the blink program

mcqs.why: The notes label the resistor as the small striped part in series with the LED, which limits its current so the LED is not damaged.

mcqs.q: What is the one visible syntax error in the printed blink program?

mcqs.why: The notes say the book claims three errors, but only one syntax error is visible: the missing semicolon after the second delay(1000); the rest is correct.

options: The program runs but the LED stays off
The delay becomes twice as long
Only the Serial Monitor stops working
The program will not compile and nothing will run
mcqs.why: The notes explain that every Arduino statement must end with a semicolon, so without it the program will not compile and nothing will run.

mcqs.q: In the corrected blink program, delay(1000) makes the LED blink once every what?
options: Once a second, because 1000 milliseconds = 1 second
Once a minute, because 1000 means 1000 seconds
Ten times a second
Once every 1000 seconds
mcqs.why: The code waits 1000 milliseconds with the LED on and 1000 milliseconds off; 1000 / 1000 = 1, so each wait is 1 second and the LED blinks once a second.

lessons.title: Design Tools and Publishing Basics
lessons.notes_html:
Digital publishing and print publishing

Digital publishing shares a design on a screen, for example posting a poster on the school website or social media, where it can be sent to friends with a click. Print publishing makes physical copies, for example printing flyers for a school event to hand out. Digital suits videos and online sharing; print suits handing a copy to someone in person.

Two key design basics for a poster

First, Colours: use two or three bright colours to grab attention, but do not mix too many, for example red and yellow for a fun event. Second, Balance and Contrast: spread things out so the poster is not crowded, and use dark text on a light background (or the reverse) so the message stands out and is easy to read.

Designs you can create with Canva

Posters for school events, presentations for class, and social media posts are three designs Canva is made for. Canva also offers flyers, brochures and other ready templates, all built from its text, elements and picture tools.

CapCut for a school event video flyer

CapCut is a video-editing tool, so it can trim clips, add transitions, music and text, and join short scenes into one lively flyer video. A moving video catches attention far better than a still notice, which is exactly what a school event announcement needs.

The documentation system for designs

A documentation system is an organized way of saving and naming design files, for example keeping a project folder with the poster, the video and a list of what was given to whom. It matters because it stops files being lost or mixed up, makes the latest version easy to find, and lets the team track printed copies and online links.

lessons.title: Design Projects in Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Creating a poster in Canva

Step 1: Open Canva and choose the Poster template size.

Step 2: Pick a background colour or picture that suits the event.

Step 3: Add the event title in a big, easy-to-read font, with the date, time and place in smaller text.

Step 4: Use Elements to add shapes, icons or pictures that match the theme, keeping two or three colours and a balanced layout.

Step 5: Check the spelling and spacing, then download the poster as a PDF for printing or as an image for sharing online.

Making a QR code and adding it to a poster

Step 1: Save the project file with a clear name, such as TalentShowPoster_Final.pdf, and upload it to Google Drive.

Step 2: Create a QR code for that Drive link using a QR generator.

Step 3: Place the QR code on the printed poster where it is easy to scan.

It is useful because anyone with a phone can scan the poster and see more details online at once, instead of the poster having to carry every detail in print.

Canva and CapCut compared

First difference: Canva is mainly for still designs such as posters, presentations and social media images, while CapCut specializes in editing videos. Second difference: Canva builds a design from templates, text and elements, while CapCut builds a video from clips, trimming, transitions and sound. For a talent show, Canva would make the poster and the printed programme, and CapCut would edit the short announcement video and the highlights video afterwards.

Barcodes for managing printed flyers

A barcode is a printed pattern of bars that a scanner can read to identify an item or a batch. For flyers, a barcode on the stack lets the team track how many copies are left.

Step 1: Print the flyers and stack them neatly.

Step 2: Generate a barcode for the batch (for example one code per class set).

Step 3: Stick or print the barcode on the stack.

Step 4: Scan it whenever copies are given out, and keep a written list, such as 10 to Class 5 and 5 to Teachers, so the remaining count is always known.

Organizing digital and print media

Organizing media matters because a lost file, a mixed-up version or an uncounted stack wastes time and can spoil the event publicity. For a school fair: save the poster and video in one named folder, with the final versions clearly marked. Upload the video to Drive and put its QR code on the printed poster so visitors can watch it by scanning. Print the posters, stack them neatly, add a barcode to each stack, and keep a list of who received copies. This way the digital files are easy to find, the printed copies are counted, and nothing is handed out twice or lost.

lessons.title: HTML, CSS and JavaScript Basics
lessons.notes_html:
The paragraph tag and paragraphs

The <p> tag marks a paragraph of text on a webpage. The browser shows its content as a block of text with a gap before and after it, so separate paragraphs stay clearly apart instead of running together.

Displaying an image with the img tag

The tag is: <img src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo">. The src attribute gives the file name (the image source), and the alt attribute gives short text that shows if the picture cannot load.

The anchor tag and hyperlinks

The <a> (anchor) tag creates a hyperlink. Its href attribute gives the address to jump to, so clicking the linked text or picture takes the visitor to another page, section or website.

A CSS rule for a green background

The rule is: body { background-color: green; }. The selector body picks the whole page, and the background-color property sets its background to green.

CSS classes: styling many elements at once

A class is defined once in CSS, for example .note { color: blue; }, and then added to any number of elements with class="note". Every element carrying that class gets the same style at once, so changing the one rule updates them all.

The getElementById function

It finds one element on the page by its id, so a script can work with that exact element. For example, getElementById("title") returns the heading with id="title", whose text or style the script can then change when a button is clicked.

E-Commerce and Daraz

E-Commerce is buying and selling things on the internet, instead of in a physical shop. Daraz is a well-known e-Commerce platform in Pakistan, where sellers list products online and buyers order and pay for them through the website or app.

Talking to the buyer after an order

Talking to the buyer confirms the order, clears up any doubt about size, colour or delivery, and builds trust. A buyer who is kept informed is far more likely to be satisfied, to accept the delivery happily, and to buy again or recommend the shop.

lessons.notes_html:
A simple shop webpage with HTML and CSS

The code:

<html>

<head>

<title>My Online Shop</title>

<style>

h1 { color: green; }

p { color: blue; }

</style>

</head>

<body>

<h1>My Online Shop</h1>

<p>Welcome to my store!</p>

</body>

</html>

The h1 rule colours the heading green, the p rule colours the paragraph blue, and the two text lines appear exactly as asked.

Changing a heading with JavaScript

Give the heading an id, for example <h1 id="title">Old Text</h1>, and add a button <button onclick="changeText()">Change</button>. Then write: function changeText() { document.getElementById("title").innerHTML = "New Text"; }. When the button is clicked, the function finds the heading by its id and replaces its text with the new text.

A simple calculator in JavaScript

Step 1: Make two number inputs and a dropdown for the operation (+, -, x, /), plus a button and a place to show the answer.

Step 2: On clicking the button, read both numbers with getElementById, check which operation was chosen, and work it out: addition adds, subtraction subtracts, multiplication multiplies, and division divides (checking that the second number is not zero, since division by zero is not allowed).

Step 3: Show the result in the answer area, for example Result: 15.

Managing payments in an online store

Careful payment management matters because mistakes lose money, upset buyers and can close a small shop: an unpaid order shipped by mistake, or a paid order forgotten, both damage trust. For a notebook shop: set up payment options (bank card or cash on delivery) on Daraz or Shopify; after each order, check that the payment is done (for example a note saying Payment Received: Rs. 400); and write down every payment, such as Ayesha paid Rs. 400 on 10 March, in a notebook or sheet. The shop name on a webpage can be shown with the heading tag, for example <h1>Notebook Shop</h1>.

Setting up an online store on Daraz

Step 1: Sign up with your email to create a seller account on Daraz.

Step 2: Add your keychains as products, with a clear photo of each design.

Step 3: Write a description and a fair price for each keychain.

Step 4: Set up payment options, such as bank card or cash on delivery, so buyers can pay safely.

Step 5: When an order comes, pack and ship the keychain, keep the buyer informed, and record the payment, for example Keychain order paid Rs. 400.

lessons.title: Maintenance Tools and Networking Basics
lessons.notes_html:
Two system tools for maintenance

Disk Cleanup, which removes unnecessary and temporary files from a hard drive, and Disk Defragmenter, which reorganizes fragmented files for faster access. Other maintenance tools in the chapter are System Restore, Safe Mode and Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE).

What Disk Defragmenter does

Over time a hard drive stores parts of one file in scattered places, which slows reading. Disk Defragmenter gathers those scattered parts together in order, so the drive reads each file in one smooth pass and the computer runs faster.

Why an SSD is never defragmented

An SSD has no moving parts and reads any stored part equally fast, so gathering fragments together gives no speed gain. Defragmenting only adds useless write cycles, which wear the drive out sooner, so SSDs must not be defragmented.

The purpose of System Restore

System Restore returns the computer's system files and settings to an earlier point in time, called a restore point, when the computer was working well. It is used to undo a bad update, a faulty driver or a wrong setting without deleting the user's personal files.

Preventing malware

Install trusted antivirus software and keep it updated so it can scan and remove malicious programs. Also avoid opening unknown email attachments or links, which is how phishing and other malware spread, and keep the operating system updated.

Static and dynamic IP addresses

A static IP address is fixed and never changes, so a device is always found at the same address, which suits servers and hosted services. A dynamic IP address is assigned fresh each time a device joins the network and may change later, which is the usual setup for home computers and phones.

Checking an IP address: the ipconfig command

On Windows, open the Command Prompt and type ipconfig, then press Enter. The result shows the computer's IP address, subnet mask and default gateway for its network connection.

Port forwarding

Port forwarding is a router setting that sends incoming traffic on a chosen port straight to one chosen device on the local network. It is useful for gaming, remote access, viewing security cameras remotely, and hosting websites or servers, because outsiders can then reach that one device through the router.

lessons.title: Maintenance and Troubleshooting in Depth
lessons.notes_html:
The importance of computer maintenance

Regular maintenance keeps a computer fast, reliable and safe, and it prevents small problems, such as a full disk or an outdated antivirus, from turning into crashes or data loss. Key tasks:

  • Removing unnecessary files with Disk Cleanup.
  • Defragmenting a hard drive (never an SSD) with Disk Defragmenter.
  • Updating the operating system and antivirus.
  • Checking the drive with the Analyze option.
  • And making restore points so a fault can be undone with System Restore.

Defragmenting a hard drive: the process

Disk Defragmenter reorganizes fragmented files on a hard drive so each file's parts sit together, which makes reading faster.

Step 1: Open Disk Defragmenter and select the drive.

Step 2: Click Analyze to check whether the drive actually needs defragmentation.

Step 3: Click Optimize (Defragment) and let it run without switching the computer off.

Step 4: Check the result and repeat only when analysis shows real fragmentation.

SSDs are excluded from this process entirely.

Troubleshooting a computer that fails to start

First, boot into Safe Mode, which starts Windows with minimal drivers, so a faulty driver or program can be found. If Safe Mode does not fix it, use Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to repair startup, or use System Restore to return to a restore point from when the computer worked. If one program is causing crashes, reinstall it, and if it still crashes, uninstall it. Keeping notes of what changed just before the fault helps pinpoint the cause.

Static and dynamic IP: advantages and disadvantages

A static IP never changes, which is an advantage for servers, cameras and remote access, since the device is always at the same address; its disadvantage is that it must be set up by hand and can be easier to target. A dynamic IP is handed out automatically and may change, which is an advantage because it needs no setup and suits most home users; its disadvantage is that the address cannot be relied on for hosting, since it may change at any time.

Port forwarding and its applications

Port forwarding tells a router to pass traffic arriving on a certain port to one specific device inside the local network, instead of blocking it. Its applications, given in the chapter, are: multiplayer games connecting smoothly; remote access, so a user can control a home computer from anywhere; viewing live security-camera footage remotely; and letting others access hosted content, such as a website or server running on a home computer.

lessons.notes_html:
AI in speech-to-text

AI speech recognition listens to spoken words, breaks the sound into patterns, and matches those patterns to words and sentences. This turns speech into written text, which is used in dictation, subtitles, voice assistants and meeting notes.

AI in video editing

AI video tools can trim clips, add transitions, pick highlights and suggest music automatically, which used to take a long editing session by hand. This lets a student or creator finish a clean, well-paced video far more quickly.

AI in image creation

AI image tools, such as DALL.E, create pictures from a written description, so a user can get an original illustration without drawing or photography. This is useful for posters, presentations and design ideas when no ready picture exists.

GitHub Copilot

GitHub Copilot is an AI coding assistant that suggests lines or whole blocks of code as a developer types. It helps developers write code faster and with fewer routine mistakes, while the developer still checks and corrects the suggestions.

AI in task automation

The main benefit is that repetitive, routine work is done quickly and without tiring, which saves time and cuts human error. People are then free for creative work, decisions and tasks that need judgement, while the machine handles the repeated steps.

AI in daily life

A voice assistant on a phone, such as one that answers questions, sets reminders or plays music on a spoken command, is AI in daily life. Other everyday examples are personalized recommendations on shopping or video apps, and grammar correction while typing.

AI in retail

Retail uses AI for personalized recommendations, suggesting products a customer is likely to want based on past browsing and buying. It also helps with stock control, demand prediction and chatbots that answer shoppers' questions at any hour.

lessons.title: AI in Society
lessons.notes_html:
AI in healthcare

AI in healthcare mainly diagnoses diseases and analyzes medical images, for example scanning X-rays or scans to spot signs of illness earlier than the eye alone might. It also helps predict patient risk, plan treatment, and manage hospital records, and chatbots can answer basic health questions. These tools support doctors and speed up care, but the final medical decision stays with a trained professional.

AI in education: advantages and limitations

Advantages: AI gives instant feedback, personalizes practice to each student's level, summarizes long texts while keeping key points, and corrects grammar and spelling. Limitations: it can be biased, it can make confident mistakes, it raises privacy questions about student data, and over-reliance on it can weaken a student's own thinking and writing. Used as a helper with teacher guidance, it strengthens learning; used as a replacement for thinking, it weakens it.

AI in transportation

Transportation uses AI for route planning and traffic prediction, so drivers and delivery fleets avoid jams and save fuel. It powers driver-assistance and self-driving systems, which use computer vision to recognize roads, vehicles and pedestrians. It also helps airlines and railways predict demand and manage schedules, making travel safer and more efficient.

AI-powered recommendation systems

A recommendation system learns from a user's past choices, searches and ratings, and from the choices of similar users. Its key features are personalization (different suggestions for different people), continuous learning (suggestions improve as more data arrives), and ranking (the most relevant items appear first). Retail shops and video apps use it to show products or videos each person is most likely to enjoy.

AI for environmental challenges

AI can analyze large environmental data, such as satellite images and weather records, to track deforestation, pollution and climate change. It helps predict floods, wildfires and crop needs, optimize energy use in buildings and grids, and plan efficient transport to cut emissions. In short, it turns huge data into early warnings and smarter use of resources.
